Definition: from G1 (as negative particle) and G1492; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls:--grave, hell.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, háidēs is the word for grave, hell. In Matthew 11:23, the text says "shalt be brought down to hell." In Luke 10:15, the text says "shalt be thrust down to hell."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that háidēs matters because death is real, but it is not the end — God has the last word over it. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; Jesus Sends Out the Seventy-Two; John's Vision of the Risen Christ on Patmos
